title: Directed etale cohomology colimits at coefficient size
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme of universe $u$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed partial order of universe $u+1$, considered as a category with an arrow $i\to j$ when $i\le j$. Let $D:I\to\mathrm{Sheaf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathrm{Ab})$ be a diagram of abelian sheaves whose section groups lie in universe $u+1$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $c$ a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each $q\ge0$, the functor $F\mapsto H^q(R\Gamma(X,F[0]))$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] maps $c$ to a colimit cocone of abelian groups, with precisely the images of its original coprojections as legs. There is no torsion assumption.

source.place: Tag 03Q5 (lemma-colimit), direct proof, with sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0739 (lemma-colim-works-over-collection), proof. Directed indices have universe u+1, the coefficient size; only finite upper bounds enter the proof.

proof.text: Let X be a qcqs scheme of universe u, and I a nonempty directed partial order of universe u+1. Let D be an I-diagram of abelian sheaves with groups in universe u+1. *Notation; the derived functors over an object.* Put $\mathcal A=\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. It is a Grothendieck abelian category [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck], so it has functorial injective embeddings $j:\mathrm{id}\to J$ [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding]; in particular it has enough injectives. For an object $U$ of $Y_{\Et}$ the functor $\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}$, $G\mapsto G(U)$, is additive and left exact (kernels in $\mathcal A$ are computed sectionwise), and $H^p(U,-)$ denotes its $p$-th right derived functor computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. For a filtered diagram $i\mapsto\mathcal F_i$, $\mathcal I\to\mathcal A$ ($\mathcal I$ a small filtered category), with colimit $(\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i,(c_i)_i)$ in $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the *canonical map* $\kappa^p_U:\varinjlim_iH^p(U,\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(U,\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i)$ is the unique homomorphism whose composite with the coprojection of $H^p(U,\mathcal F_i)$ is $H^p(U,c_i)$ (the $H^p(U,c_i)$ form a cocone because $H^p(U,-)$ is a functor).

source.place: Section Tag 0737 (label section-limits), first paragraph: the canonical map; Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 0739 (label lemma-colim-works-over-collection) and its proof, second paragraph (functorial injective embeddings, Injectives Theorem Tag 01DP)

proof.text: *The set $\mathcal B$ and the coverings $\mathrm{Cov}$.* Let $\mathcal B$ be the set of objects $U\to X$ of $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] whose scheme $U$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $\mathrm{Cov}$ the set of coverings $\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ of $Y_{\Et}$ with $T$ finite and $U,U_t\in\mathcal B$. (a) $X\in\mathcal B$: $\mathrm{id}_Y$ is an open immersion, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), and $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by hypothesis. (b) For $\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}\in\mathrm{Cov}$ every $U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_p}$ ($p\ge0$) lies in $\mathcal B$. These fibre products in $Y_{\Et}$ are the scheme-theoretic ones [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Induction on $p$, the case $p=0$ being $U_{t_0}\in\mathcal B$. For $p\ge1$ put $W=U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_{p-1}}\in\mathcal B$. The morphism $U_{t_p}\to U$ is quasi-compact ($U_{t_p}$ quasi-compact, $U$ quasi-separated) and quasi-separated ($U_{t_p}$ quasi-separated) by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1). So its base change $W\times_UU_{t_p}\to W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by (3) of the same node. As $W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so is $W\times_UU_{t_p}$, by (2). (c) For $U\in\mathcal B$ the coverings of $U$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$ are cofinal among all coverings of $U$ in $Y_{\Et}$. Let $\{T_a\to U\}_{a\in A}$ be a covering (jointly surjective, the $T_a\to U$ etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3)). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-cofinal-finite-coverings] there are a finite set $B$, affine schemes $V_b$ and etale maps $V_b\to U$ factoring through $T_{a(b)}\to U$, jointly surjective. Each $V_b\to U\to X$ is etale (composite of etale morphisms, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2)), so $V_b$ is an object of $Y_{\Et}$. $V_b$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $V_b\in\mathcal B$. Hence $\{V_b\to U\}_{b\in B}\in\mathrm{Cov}$, and it refines $\{T_a\to U\}$. Thus $(\mathcal B,\mathrm{Cov})$ satisfies hypotheses (1) and (2) of Stacks 0739 (and of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion]), with all coverings in $\mathrm{Cov}$ finite.

source.place: Cohomology of Spaces, Lemma Tag 073E (label lemma-colimits), proof: the choice of $\mathcal B$ as the quasi-compact quasi-separated objects, cofinality of finite coverings, and the qcqs permanence (there Morphisms of Spaces 03KS; for schemes Schemes 03GI, 01KV, 01K5, 01KU)

proof.text: *Degree $0$.* For $U\in\mathcal B$ and every filtered diagram $(\mathcal F_i)$ in $\mathcal A$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i(U)\to(\varinjlim_i\mathcal F_i)(U)$ is bijective. This is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-qcqs-sections-filtered-colimit] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$: a sheaf of $\mathbf Z_Y$-modules is the same as an abelian sheaf, and $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\mathbf Z)=\mathcal A$ with the same colimits. Composing with the natural isomorphism $R^0v\cong v$ for the left exact functor $v=(-)(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2), $\kappa^0_U$ is an isomorphism for all $U\in\mathcal B$ and all filtered diagrams.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 0739 (label lemma-colim-works-over-collection) and its proof, first paragraph (the case $p=0$ via Sites, Lemma Tag 0738 (4))

proof.text: *The injective diagram and its colimit.* Let $(\mathcal F_i)_{i\in\mathcal I}$ be a filtered diagram in $\mathcal A$. Put $\mathcal I_i=J(\mathcal F_i)$ and $\mathcal Q_i=\operatorname{Coker}(j_{\mathcal F_i})$, with the maps induced by functoriality. By [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding] the $j_{\mathcal F_i}$ form a morphism of diagrams $(\mathcal F_i)\to(\mathcal I_i)$. Each $j_{\mathcal F_i}$ is a monomorphism and each $\mathcal I_i$ is injective. Cokernels are functorial, so $(\mathcal Q_i)$ is a filtered diagram and $0\to\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal I_i\to\mathcal Q_i\to0$ is a diagram of short exact sequences. Filtered colimits in $\mathcal A$ exist and are exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact], so $0\to\varinjlim\mathcal F_i\to\varinjlim\mathcal I_i\to\varinjlim\mathcal Q_i\to0$ is short exact. The coprojections form a morphism of short exact sequences from each $0\to\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal I_i\to\mathcal Q_i\to0$ to it.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 0739 (label lemma-colim-works-over-collection) and its proof, second paragraph

proof.text: *Claim: $H^q(U,\varinjlim_i\mathcal I_i)=0$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$ and $q\ge1$.* Put $\mathcal G=\varinjlim_i\mathcal I_i$. We check hypothesis (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion] for $(\mathcal B,\mathrm{Cov})$; (1) and (2) hold by step 2. Let $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}\in\mathrm{Cov}$. In degree $p$ the Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex] is $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=\prod_{(t_0,\ldots,t_p)\in T^{p+1}}\mathcal G(U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_p})$, a finite product since $T$ is finite. Each fibre product lies in $\mathcal B$ (step 2 (b)), so by step 3 each factor is $\varinjlim_i\mathcal I_i(U_{t_0\cdots t_p})$, compatibly with restriction maps. A finite product of abelian groups is a finite direct sum, and colimits commute with direct sums. Hence $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=\varinjlim_i\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$ as complexes, the differentials being alternating sums of restriction maps. Each $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal I_i)$ is exact in degrees $\ge1$, since $\mathcal I_i$ is injective in $\mathcal A$ [lem-weil-pbc-injective-sheaf-cech-acyclic]. A filtered colimit of complexes of abelian groups exact at a degree is exact there [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. So $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=0$ for $p>0$. Then [lem-weil-pbc-cech-vanishing-criterion] gives $H^q(U,\mathcal G)=0$ for $q>0$ and all $U\in\mathcal B$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 0739 (label lemma-colim-works-over-collection) and its proof, last paragraph (the claim, via Lemma Tag 03F9 (lemma-cech-vanish-collection) and Lemma Tag 03AW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech))

proof.text: *Induction on $p$: $\kappa^p_U$ is an isomorphism for all $p\ge0$, all $U\in\mathcal B$ and all filtered diagrams.* The case $p=0$ is step 3. Assume it for $p$ (all $U\in\mathcal B$, all filtered diagrams), fix $U\in\mathcal B$ and $(\mathcal F_i)$, and use steps 4 and 5. The derived functors $H^n(U,-)$ form a $\delta$-functor whose long exact sequences have connecting maps $\delta_S$ natural in the short exact sequence $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (1), (2) (the exactness is also [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact]). Also $H^n(U,\mathcal I_i)=0$ for $n>0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing]. This gives, for each $i$, an exact sequence $H^p(U,\mathcal I_i)\to H^p(U,\mathcal Q_i)\to H^{p+1}(U,\mathcal F_i)\to0$. These sequences are compatible with the transition maps by naturality of $\delta$. Their filtered colimit $\varinjlim H^p(U,\mathcal I_i)\to\varinjlim H^p(U,\mathcal Q_i)\to\varinjlim H^{p+1}(U,\mathcal F_i)\to0$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. For the colimit sequence of step 4 one gets the exact sequence $H^p(U,\varinjlim\mathcal I_i)\to H^p(U,\varinjlim\mathcal Q_i)\to H^{p+1}(U,\varinjlim\mathcal F_i)\to H^{p+1}(U,\varinjlim\mathcal I_i)=0$, the last group being $0$ by step 5. The vertical maps $\kappa^p_U$ (for $(\mathcal I_i)$ and $(\mathcal Q_i)$) and $\kappa^{p+1}_U$ (for $(\mathcal F_i)$) make the two rows commute. To see this, check on each coprojection from $H^\ast(U,-_i)$. There the first square is functoriality of $H^p(U,-)$. The second square is the naturality of $\delta^p$ for the morphism of short exact sequences given by the coprojections (step 4) [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (1). By the induction hypothesis the first two vertical maps are isomorphisms. A diagram chase (the five lemma with zeros on the right) then shows that the third map $\kappa^{p+1}_U$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma]. Explicitly, surjectivity: lift a class through $H^p(U,\varinjlim\mathcal Q_i)$. Injectivity: a class mapping to $0$ comes from $\varinjlim H^p(U,\mathcal Q_i)$; its image in $H^p(U,\varinjlim\mathcal Q_i)$ comes from $H^p(U,\varinjlim\mathcal I_i)$, hence from $\varinjlim H^p(U,\mathcal I_i)$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 0739 (label lemma-colim-works-over-collection) and its proof, second paragraph (the commutative diagram and the snake lemma)

proof.text: *Identification with the cohomology of the statement.* Take $U=X\in\mathcal B$ (step 2 (a)). $X$ is the final object of $Y_{\Et}$, so $G\mapsto G(X)$ is the global sections functor $\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\mathcal A$. By [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], $H^q(Y_{\Et},F)=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(X,I^\bullet))$ for a K-injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], independent of the choice [prop-weil-pbc-cohomology-resolution-independent]. This is $\mathcal H^q(R\Gamma(X,F[0]))$. A morphism $\varphi$ induces $H^q(\varphi)$ through a lift to the resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. By [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification] (with $v=\Gamma(X,-)$, $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck abelian) there is an isomorphism $\theta^q_F:H^q(Y_{\Et},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X,F)=R^q\Gamma(X,F)$. It is natural in $F$, both sides being functorial through lifts of $\varphi$ to resolutions, unique up to homotopy. By naturality, $\theta^q$ carries the maps $H^q(Y_{\Et},c_a)$ to $H^q(X,c_a)$. So it carries the canonical map $\varinjlim_aH^q(Y_{\Et},F_a)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},\varinjlim_aF_a)$ of the statement (induced by the $H^q(c_a)$) to $\kappa^q_Y$, up to the isomorphisms $\varinjlim_a\theta^q_{F_a}$ and $\theta^q_{\varinjlim F_a}$. By step 6 it is bijective for every $q\ge0$. No torsion hypothesis was used. All constructions use filtered colimits in abelian groups and sheaves at universe u+1, and only finite upper bounds in I; no shrinking of I to universe u is needed. The resulting comparison sends each coprojection to its derived cohomology map, so it proves the IsColimit assertion for the supplied cocone.
